facts.statement: Bonatitan is a titanosaurian dinosaur found in the Late Cretaceous Allen Formation of Argentina.
facts.quote: Bonatitan is a genus of titanosaurian dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Allen Formation of Argentina.

facts.statement: The genus Bonatitan was named in 2004.
The type species Bonatitan reigi was first described by Martinelli and Forasiepi in 2004.
facts.quote: The type species is Bonatitan reigi, first described by Martinelli and Forasiepi in 2004.

facts.statement: The genus name honors paleontologist José Fernando Bonaparte and the species name honors Osvaldo Reig.
facts.quote: The genus and species names honor the famous Argentine paleontologists José Fernando Bonaparte and Osvaldo Reig.

facts.statement: Bonatitan lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 83 to 65 million years ago, in the Campanian and Maastrichtian stages.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 83 y 65 millones de años, en el Campaniense y el Maastrichtiense

facts.statement: Bonatitan lived in what is now South America.
facts.quote: en lo que hoy es Sudamérica.

facts.statement: Bonatitan was a lightly built sauropod measuring about 6 meters long, 1.5 meters high, and weighing 3 tons.
facts.quote: Bonatitan es un saurópodo muy ligeramente construido de cerca de 6 metros de largo, 1,5 de alto y un peso de 3 toneladas

facts.statement: Bonatitan possessed uniform cavities in its caudal vertebrae.
facts.quote: con las cavidades uniformes en las vértebras caudales.

facts.statement: Bonatitan fossils were found in the Río Colorado Subgroup at Bajo Santa Rosa in Río Negro Province, Argentina.
facts.quote: Sus restos fueron encontrados en el Subgrupo Río Colorado, en el área de Bajo Santa Rosa, en la Provincia del Río Negro en la Argentina.

facts.statement: Bonatitan was described from two incomplete skeletons including the base of the skull by Martinelli and Forasiepi in 2004.
facts.quote: Fue descrito a partir de dos esqueletos incompletos con la presencia de la base del cráneo, por Martinelli y Forasiepi en el 2004.

facts.statement: Bonatitan is classified within the family Saltasauridae.
Bonatitan belongs to the parent group Saltasaurinae.
José Bonaparte discovered the remains of Bonatitan in 1990.
facts.quote: El nombre del género es en honor al paleontólogo argentino José Bonaparte, quien lo descubrió en 1990

facts.statement: Researchers suggest there may be a sauropod taxon in the Allen Formation distinct from Bonatitan, though this remains possible evidence rather than a confirmed discovery.
facts.quote: providing possible evidence of presence of a sauropod taxon distinct from Aeolosaurus rionegrinus, Bonatitan, Menucocelsior and Rocasaurus in the Allen Formation.
